Global home — the fleet-wide dashboard

The landing page of the Global ADOM — infrastructure health, one card per product ADOM, active jobs, certificate expiry, shortcuts to the fleet-wide sections and a table of every appliance.

👤 ForViewerOperatorAdministrator
🔑 Permissionsappliances.view users.manage appliances.view_maintenance audit.view
📍 WhereGlobal ADOM → sidebar → Global → Dashboard (URL /)

What is it?#

The Global page is SATOM's home: the first page after sign-in and the target of the address /. It summarises the whole fleet — every product ADOM — on one screen and links to the places you go next.

What does it do?#

  • Infrastructure health — the state of the SATOM installation itself: the HA nodes (role, CPU, memory, disk), the Git repository and the backup server.
  • ADOM cards — one card per active product ADOM, with the number of appliances you can see. Clicking a card enters that ADOM.
  • Jobs card — the number of active jobs; opens the job list.
  • Certificates card — the number of device certificates SATOM knows and how many expire within 30 days; for administrators it opens the Certificate Manager.
  • Global sections — buttons to the fleet-wide pages.
  • Fleet table — every appliance you can see, from every product (needs appliances.view).

Requirements#

  • You are signed in. Visiting / always switches the current tab to the Global ADOM.
  • Appliances appear once they are registered (see Quick start).

Permissions#

Any signed-in user can open the page. What it shows depends on you:

  • The Fleet table and the appliance counts on the ADOM cards need appliances.view. Without it the table says Appliance inventory not available — Your profile does not include viewing appliances. and the cards count 0.
  • Appliances in maintenance mode are counted and listed only for users with appliances.view_maintenance.
  • The Certificate Manager, Appliances, Audit Log, Users and Database buttons under Global sections are shown only to administrators (users.manage), and each only when you can open that page (the Audit Log also requires audit.view).
  • The other buttons are shown only when your profile can open the page behind them.

ℹ️Note

Changed in 2.11.0: the Fleet table lists appliances only for users with appliances.view, and Global sections hides buttons whose page your profile cannot open.

How to use#

Read the dashboard#

  1. Open the Global ADOM: click the brand in the top bar while in Global, ‹ Global in any product sidebar, or browse to /.
  2. Check the Infrastructure health strip at the top. It loads a moment after the page (it probes the nodes and services in the background) and shows updated … when done.
  3. Read the cards: appliances per ADOM, active job(s), and certificates — N expiring ≤30d is highlighted in amber when anything expires soon.
  4. Scroll to Fleet for the full appliance table.

Jump to work#

  • Click an ADOM card to enter that product's ADOM.
  • Click Open (arrow icon) on a fleet row to open that appliance in its own ADOM; FortiWeb appliances open their appliance detail page.
  • Use Global sections: Monitoring, Search, Service Diagram, Analysis, Fleet Objects, Metrics, Jobs (and, for administrators, Certificate Manager, Appliances, Audit Log, Users, Database).
  • Switch product (top right of the page header) opens the product chooser.

Configuration#

The Fleet table columns:

Field Description Required Example
Name The appliance name in SATOM. — fweb-01
Product Product badge; a grey badge with a raw key means no active ADOM manages that kind. — FortiWeb
Host Management address and port. — 192.0.2.10:443
Zone / Line / Department Classification set on the appliance. — dmz / web / ops
Open Opens the appliance in its ADOM. — —

Example#

🧪Example — Morning check

You open SATOM and land on Global. Infrastructure health shows both nodes primary and standby reachable. The FortiWeb card shows 12 appliances, the Jobs card 2 active job(s) (last night's backups still finishing), and the Certificates card 3 expiring ≤30d in amber. You click the Certificates card to plan renewals, then use the FortiWeb card to start your policy work.

Result#

The page itself never contacts an appliance. Counts come from SATOM's inventory; the infrastructure strip is fetched separately after the page has rendered.

Troubleshooting#

"No appliances registered yet"#

Possible causes - Nothing has been registered. - Everything registered is in maintenance mode and you may not see maintenance devices.

Solution — register an appliance under Appliances (the link in the message, or Administrator → Appliances in the sidebar; without the administrator capability, Global → Appliances). See Quick start.

"Appliance inventory not available"#

Possible causes — your profile does not include appliances.view.

Solution — ask an administrator to add View appliances to your profile.

Verification — the product card shows a count above 0.

An appliance is missing from the Fleet table#

Possible causes — it is in maintenance mode and you lack appliances.view_maintenance.

Solution — ask an administrator, or check the Appliances page with an account that has the permission.

Infrastructure health shows "probe failed" or "unreachable"#

Possible causes - The peer node, the Git repository or the backup server is down or unreachable from this node. - They are not configured. The Backup server card then says not configured and Settings → Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server (a link to that tab for administrators).

Solution — open High availability for the peer node, or check Source of Truth & Backup → Backup Server (and Configuration SoT) in Settings.

The Jobs card shows 0 although a job is running#

Possible causes — the job store could not be read; the card falls back to 0 instead of breaking the page.

Solution — open Jobs directly to see the list.

Advanced#

Advanced How the cards are built
  • The ADOM cards are generated from the ADOM registry, so a product declared in Settings → ADOMs gets its card and its fleet rows without any change to the page.
  • An appliance whose product key matches no active ADOM is visible on Global only, and is listed after the others.
  • The certificate card counts every device certificate row whose expiry is within 30 days of now (UTC), including already-expired ones.
  • The infrastructure data endpoint answers only in the Global ADOM.
